subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Multi-Factor Authentication Testing
description: A fast breakdown of Multi-Factor Authentication Testing for builders.

hook.text: A password is stolen via phishing. But the attacker can't log in because they lack the second factor.

buildup.text: MFA requires two or more verification methods: something you know, have, or are.

discovery.text: Testing MFA covers bypass attempts, fallback mechanisms, and recovery flow security.

twist.text: Weak MFA implementations let attackers bypass the second factor through account recovery flows.

climax.text: Testing reveals the SMS recovery bypass. Switching to app-based tokens with secure recovery closes the gap.

punchline.text: MFA is only strong if the bypass paths are equally protected.

quiz.question: What is a common MFA weakness?
options: Insecure account recovery flows that bypass MFA
